2607.28146.title: Can Agents Deceive? Evaluating Reasoning and Deception in ParliamentBench using a Social Deduction Game
2607.28146.paper_summary: As large language models (LLMs) are deployed as agents in high-stakes settings, such as medical and legal systems, understanding their deceptive capabilities is fundamental to safety. Controlled social deduction games provide a reproducible proxy for isolating and evaluating these complex adversarial behaviors. We present the open-source benchmark framework ParliamentBench based on the game Secret Hitler to evaluate LLMs in scenarios that require deception, persuasion, and reasoning under information asymmetry. We evaluate 16 LLMs across 1,600 simulated matches playing each other, playing against humans, and compare them against a large set of online games. We introduce three novel metrics that isolate social deduction, reasoning, and deceptive consistency. Our experiments reveal that frontier models achieve strong performance across cooperative and deceptive roles, with a strong top-four cluster (GPT-5.4, Kimi K2.5, Grok 4.1 Fast, and DeepSeek 3.1 Terminus), whereas the weakest models fall short of random (33%) and simple algorithmic (45%) baselines. Most LLMs struggle to maintain a consistent deceptive persona throughout an entire game, with deception retention dropping below 50%.
2607.28146.paper_summary_zh: 隨著大型語言模型（LLMs）在高風險環境中被部署為代理，例如醫療和法律系統，理解它們的欺騙能力對於安全至關重要。受控的社會推理遊戲提供了一個可重複的代理，用於隔離和評估這些複雜的對抗行為。我們提出了基於遊戲《秘密希特勒》的開源基準框架 ParliamentBench，以評估 LLM 在需要欺騙、說服和在信息不對稱下推理的情境中的表現。我們在 1,600 場模擬比賽中評估了 16 個 LLM，這些比賽中它們互相對戰、與人類對戰，並將其與大量在線遊戲進行比較。我們引入了三個新穎的指標，分別隔離社會推理、推理和欺騙一致性。我們的實驗顯示，前沿模型在合作和欺騙角色中表現出色，形成了一個強大的前四名集群（GPT-5.4、Kimi K2.5、Grok 4.1 Fast 和 DeepSeek 3.1 Terminus），而最弱的模型則未能達到隨機（33%）和簡單算法（45%）的基準。大多數 LLM 在整個遊戲中難以保持一致的欺騙角色，欺騙保留率下降至 50% 以下。
